subject: Staff Spotlight: priority lenses & QBR commitments
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staff Spotlight: priority lenses & QBR commitments

Team —

Quick weekly readout as we lock into QBR prep. I wanted to surface the high-level wins, the near-term risks, and the immediate asks so leadership has one place to scan before Monday's prep meeting. I’ve attached a short deck + an OKR heatmap (draft).

Wins (last 7 days)
- Production rollout: Redwood-Serve v1.3 went live on dedicated pools — 12% lower p99 latency for 512-token requests vs. canary. Initial telemetry looks stable.
- Partnership: ACME PoC passed the security dry-run; API keys issued for their sandbox. Elaine said they’ll start integration tests next week.
- Observability: Console trace sampling enabled for critical routes; aggregated traces now surface request-level cost at token granularity.

Risks / Chokepoints
- Capacity: Dedicated cluster 3 has intermittent GPU OOMs under sustained batching at 2k concurrent streams. Root cause suspected in a new kernel selection path for quantized kernels. This could affect SLAs if a burst coincides with a high-concurrency job.
- QBR narrative: Our cost-optimization story needs a clearer before/after for batching + cache changes — product needs clearer numbers to present to finance.
- ACME timeline: They start integration tests Tue — if we don’t prioritize the KV-cache regression fix, they could see increased token cost in their timing windows.

Asks (actionable, assigned where possible)
- Karthik: prioritize a triage on cluster 3 OOMs — please coordinate with Infra kernel team and flag fixes for the canary by EOD Monday.
- Monica: can you finalize the cost delta slides using last-30d telemetry and drop into the deck? Need numbers by Monday 12:00pm PT.
- Laura: would appreciate a short bullet to the QBR narrative about how Dedicated differentiates on predictable latency — 2–3 lines is fine, I’ll place it on slide 3.

Attachments: QBR_priorities_v2.pdf (draft), OKR_heatmap.xlsx (draft)

Notes: I intentionally kept the heatmap coarse; we should agree on the 3 needle movers for the quarter during the prep huddle.

Thanks —
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staff Spotlight: priority lenses & QBR commitments

Chloe —

Ack and on it. Quick notes:
- I’ll spin up an isolated repro on the same model shard and reproduce the OOM; initial triage suggests a small edge-case in the attention kernel that inflates KV cache memory under certain packing heuristics. If that's confirmed, a control-plane switch to a safer packing mode is low-risk and can be rolled to canary.
- I’ll target a canary config by EOD Monday and will post updates to OPS-421.

One ask for you: can you add the specific customer windows (timezone, expected peak windows) to the ACME bullet so we prioritize the right burst profile?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Infrastructure

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 12:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staff Spotlight: priority lenses & QBR commitments

Chloe —

Thanks for the concise readout; appreciate the action orientation. A couple of prep notes:
- For the QBR narrative, two bullets: 1) "Dedicated pools + kernel-level tuning reduced p99 latency by ~12% for mid-length sequences, improving SLO compliance predictability." 2) "Cache/batching improvements reduced per-token cost for steady workloads; we recommend conservative projections for bursty enterprise customers." Keep them short on the slide; we can expand in the appendix.
- On ACME: Elaine told me they plan integration runs 08:00–11:00 PT Tue and Thu this sprint. If Karthik can prioritize the packing-mode control-plane switch before Tuesday morning, that should eliminate their primary cost spike.
- Monica: happy to review the cost delta numbers once you have the sheet.

Also — small org ask: can we pull one example trace (anonymized) that shows the before/after batching effect? That will make the cost story concrete for finance. Please add to the drive link.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM Strategy & Operations

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staff Spotlight: priority lenses & QBR commitments

Laura / Karthik / Monica —

Thanks — quick status update and next steps consolidated into one place: 
1) Karthik: OPS-421 created; triage started. Please use the canary flagging plan and post the canary config to the Jira ticket. Prioritize Tuesday 06:00 PT canary if feasible (matches ACME window).
2) Monica: I pulled a draft trace and placed it in the Drive folder (see link). Please drop the cost delta numbers into OKR_heatmap.xlsx and update the deck. If you need a sample of anonymized request IDs to pull traces, ping infra — I left a note on OPS-421.
3) Laura: I inserted your two bullets into slide 3 (see QBR_priorities_v2.pdf in Drive). If anything needs to be softened/tightened, let me know — final deck freeze Monday 5pm PT.

ACME liaison: Elaine, looping you in here so you're aware of the action plan. We aim to have the canary change in place before your Tuesday integration window; I’ll confirm once Karthik verifies.

Forwarding attachments (stubs): QBR_priorities_v2.pdf, OKR_heatmap.xlsx

Thanks everyone — short huddle Monday 09:00 PT (15m) to lock slides and speaker assignments.

-Chloe
Chloe Martin
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
